scholarships.title: Hanns-Seidel-Stiftung Scholarship – Förderung internationaler Studierender und Promovierender (Scholarship for Studies / PhDs for international students and doctoral candidates)
scholarships.official_source: Hanns-Seidel-Stiftung e. V., Institut für Begabtenförderung

eligibility: I am less than 45 years old
I have proof of German language skills of at least B2 or a comparable level
I show above-average performance at school or in my studies
I am actively involved in voluntary work (politics, church, social association, sports, music, etc.)
I support democracy, rule of law, and human rights
I speak German at an adequate level
I complete a full-time course of study at a state or state-recognized university in Germany
existing.eligibility_summary: Under 45, proven German skills of at least B2 or comparable, above-average performance, voluntary engagement, political interest, civic-mindedness, acceptance of the foundation's aims, and a full-time course of study at a state or state-recognised higher education institution in Germany.
benefits: Monthly study scholarship of at most 992 €/month calculated according to BMBF guidelines, the level depending on the income and assets of the person responsible for support (page 'Finanzielle Förderung')

Study-cost flat rate of 300 €/month paid in addition to and independently of parents' income, intended for study-related expenditure that does not serve subsistence – for example learning and working materials (including books, hardware and software), language courses, relevant specialist conferences, congress visits and excursions
coverage: Monthly study scholarship of at most 992 €/month calculated according to BMBF guidelines, the level depending on the income and assets of the person responsible for support (page 'Finanzielle Förderung')

Study-cost flat rate of 300 €/month paid in addition to and independently of parents' income, intended for study-related expenditure that does not serve subsistence – for example learning and working materials (including books, hardware and software), language courses, relevant specialist conferences, congress visits and excursions
requirements: Applications can be submitted only through the HSS application portal; incomplete applications cannot be submitted
Scholarship holders receive an electronic confirmation that the application has been submitted; no separate confirmation email is sent
Applicants from countries where the HSS maintains a country office must contact that office first; where no office exists, the application is submitted directly via the online application portal
Selection presupposes a preliminary screening in the Institute for Talent Promotion and, for shortlisted candidates, an invitation to a selection meeting
The applicant is informed by email about the outcome and any next steps approximately four weeks after the application deadline
documents: Detailed curriculum vitae (PDF file): same facts as the tabular CV but allowing reasons for decisions and formative events; length two to four pages, margins 2.5 cm, line spacing 1.5
One-page exposé on study and career goals (PDF file)
If available: interim diploma/Bachelor certificate (PDF file)
If available: current transcript of grades (PDF file) or graded/ungraded university certificates (combined into one PDF file)
Certificate(s) of voluntary engagement, combined into one PDF file, using the published template

Expert opinion (Fachgutachten) from a (junior) professor, a Privatdozent/in or in justified exceptional cases a doctoral academic employee, assessing the specialist qualification; for students in the first or possibly second semester the opinion may come from a teacher. An English version of the expert opinion template is also published
If available: current registration certificate or admission certificate (PDF file – can be submitted later by first-year students)
For international students: proof of German language skills of at least B2 or a comparable level – applications without proof of German language skills are not considered
application_method: Check the requirements for your programme on the 'Wen wir suchen' page and confirm every point with 'yes'
Contact the HSS country office in your home country, or, if the HSS has no office there, go directly to the application portal
Prepare all documents listed under the relevant programme section as PDF files before starting
Submit the application exclusively via the HSS application portal between 15 December 2026 and 15 January 2027 (12:00 CET)
Submit on the portal: the portal only allows submission when all mandatory fields are complete; you can save and resume an application until it is submitted
existing.selection_notes: A preliminary screening is carried out in the Institute für Begabtenförderung against the criteria on the 'Wen wir suchen' page. Applicants who appear suitable are invited to a selection meeting (Auswahltagung) where they are examined by an independent selection committee. The outcome and any next steps are communicated by email about four weeks after the closing date.
existing.best_fit: International students already enrolled in, or about to enrol in, a full-time degree programme at a state or state-recognised university in Germany, who are under 45, can prove German at B2 level or equivalent, have above-average school or study performance, are involved in voluntary work, are politically interested and endorse the foundation's aims. For doctoral candidates: admitted to a German university or research institution.
existing.notes: The scholarship does not have to be repaid. There is no legal entitlement to the stated benefits; the amount is individually calculated. Double funding by the Hanns-Seidel-Stiftung together with BAföG or other public funds is excluded. Study scholarship holders drop out of the study funding programme on passing their first qualifying examination, although they remain connected to HSS as former scholarship holders. Promotion funding ends in the month of the last examination or defence of the dissertation, and is initially granted for three years, with a six-month extension possible on justified application and up to a maximum of four years in exceptional cases such as illness or pregnancy. The published pages do not state a deferral rule.
existing.duration: Study scholarship: normally up to the maximum funding period under BAföG, reviewed at the end of each funding year; doctoral scholarship: initially three years, extendable by six months on justified application and in exceptional cases up to a maximum of four years
existing.application_period: 15 December 2026 – 15 January 2027 (12:00 CET) and, for the same programme, 15 June 2027 – 15 July 2027 (12:00 CEST); the Institute informs applicants by email about the outcome of their application approximately four weeks after the application deadline
existing.deadline_display: Application portal open 15 December 2026 to 15 January 2027 inclusive (12:00 CET) for Internationale Studierende und Promovierende (Ausländer); a further window 15 June 2027 to 15 July 2027 (12:00 CEST). Applications possible only via the HSS online application portal.

scholarships.title: Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung Promotionsförderung für Ausländer:innen (FES doctoral scholarship for international doctoral candidates)

existing.description: The Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung funds doctoral candidates from abroad who are admitted to a German university, paying 1,500 euros a month plus a supplement for statutory health insurance, together with an extensive political education programme. Applicants must have very good German skills (B2 accepted, also without a certificate, and required even when the dissertation is written in English), socio-political engagement, identification with the values of social democracy, an above-average and fast degree result, and a research project that makes a significant contribution to research. The scholarship does not have to be repaid.
eligibility: You are admitted to doctoral study at a German higher education institution
You have very good German language skills
You identify with the values of social democracy
You completed your degree with an above-average result and promptly
Your research project makes a significant contribution to research
With the exception of doctorates in medicine, doctoral projects in all subjects are funded
existing.eligibility_summary: Doctoral candidates from abroad admitted to a German higher education institution, with very good German skills (B2 accepted even without certificate), socio-political engagement, identification with the values of social democracy, an above-average and fast degree result, and a research project making a significant contribution to research; all disciplines except medicine.
benefits: Extensive offer of seminars, workshops and competence training
Networking in interdisciplinary doctoral colloquia for doctoral scholarship holders
Specialist conferences with experts from politics and science on selected socio-political topics, with the opportunity to present individual dissertation projects
Scholarship-holder groups in numerous cities and 18 cross-city thematic working groups
Integration into the network of current and former scholarship holders, with former holders acting as mentors
Refusal of travel costs incurred for a selection interview can be reimbursed via the published travel-cost form
Where engagement only started recently, applicants are invited to describe their previous engagement, including in their country of origin
coverage: Monthly payment of 1,500 euros to doctoral scholarship holders of the Promotionsförderung für Ausländer:innen
A supplement for statutory health insurance (Zuschuss zur gesetzlichen Krankenversicherung)
requirements: Applications must be submitted in German, because German language skills are a requirement for the scholarship
You must already be studying in Germany at the time of your application and be admitted to doctoral study
Proof of German language skills is absolutely necessary and must be provided; B2 is accepted also without a certificate
You have three weeks to submit your documents and up to six weeks for the expert opinions after the request
From the application to the decision it can take three to seven months

The foundation does not fund, outside an existing FES scholarship: short-term stays abroad, project proposals, short-term courses of study (fewer than three semesters, e.g. two-semester Master's programmes), research visits, trainee programmes, Studienkolleg, medical studies before the Physikum, doctorates and further medical training, pure final phases of a degree or doctorate, postdoc projects, physiotherapist training, purely foreign degree programmes outside the EU, part-time or extra-occupational study, language courses, internships and summer schools, and second degrees
documents: Detailed curriculum vitae with information on previous education and socio-political engagement
Certificates, university entrance qualification, registration certificate, other evidence
Two expert opinions (Gutachten) from university teachers; for first-year students, from teachers
Online application form (Promotionsförderung für Ausländer:innen) at the FES application portal
application_method: Choose the matching online application form for your scholarship programme

Fill in the online application form with general personal information, professional and family background, your motivation to become an FES scholarship holder, and details of your socio-political engagement
Within two to four weeks of receipt, receive either a rejection or the request to submit your documents and expert opinions
Submit the documents and the two expert opinions; you receive confirmation of receipt
If shortlisted, attend the first specialist interview with a trust lecturer (Vertrauensdozentin/Vertrauensdozent)
If shortlisted again, attend the second interview with a member of the selection committee
Final decision by the selection committee, communicated at the latest one week after the meeting
existing.selection_notes: The FES checks the online application for formal and content criteria. In selecting, it particularly considers applications from people who are the first in their family to study and/or have a migration background, as well as from women and from students at universities of applied sciences and in MINT subjects. Suitable applicants are passed to a trust lecturer for a specialist interview that produces an opinion; shortlisted applicants then have a second interview with a member of the selection committee, whose opinion goes to the committee's meeting. The selection committee meets eight to ten times a year and decides on admission; the applicant is informed at the latest one week after the meeting. All applicants are informed by email at each stage. 'Above average' refers to the average grade in the subject at the university location or in the training occupation.
existing.best_fit: Doctoral candidates who came from abroad, are admitted to a German university, write their dissertation in German (or English, with German skills anyway), have completed their degree with an above-average result and quickly, are socio-politically engaged, and identify with social democracy.
existing.notes: The scholarship does not have to be repaid. Funding lasts three and a half years as a rule, can be extended in justified exceptional cases, and in any case no longer than the final examination. The award is discontinued at the latest with the final examination. Income exceeding 400 euros per month is credited against the scholarship, according to the Foundation's English information page. Applications for the Promotionsförderung für Ausländer:innen require German language skills even where the dissertation is written in English. Medicine is excluded.
existing.duration: As a rule three and a half years; in justified exceptional cases it can be granted for longer, but at the latest until the final examination
existing.application_period: Continuous/rolling: applications are accepted while the doctoral thesis can still be completed within the funding period, in principle from about two years before submission of the dissertation. The selection committee meets eight to ten times a year and the final decision is communicated at the latest one week after the relevant meeting.
existing.deadline_display: No fixed calendar deadline is published. The programme page states the right time to apply is up to about two years before submission of the dissertation ('bis circa zwei Jahre vor Abgabe der Dissertation'), and the application page directs applicants to the individual scholarship programme for the deadlines. The online application form for Promotionsförderung für Ausländer:innen is published and open.
